subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP/sub-agent thread messages bypass busy channel or reply-operation admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a successor be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent routing contract affects message ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Refresh Admission Fix
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a rebased successor as the canonical path, fixing accepted-queue fallback semantics and preserving terminal recovery.

options.title: Limit To Explicit Controls
options.body: Keep ordinary messages queued for now and document command-only steering until maintainers choose a safer active-session ingress design.

options.title: Split Channel Follow-Ups
options.body: Keep the broader queue-steering issue canonical and retain Discord ACP/thread-specific validation as a separate follow-up only if the generic admission fix is insufficient.

recommendation.title: Refresh Admission Fix
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 or a rebased successor as the canonical path, fixing accepted-queue fallback semantics and preserving terminal recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the latest current-main partial steering fix and are positioned to judge whether a successor should preserve or change that behavior.
